A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OSCP/GAND/CAP research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables support comparison despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet and CelebA-HQ experiments, purification timings, ablations, image-quality measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations against L2-PGD, StAdv, Snow, and Fog in Appendix Table 11.

M1.justification: The GAND and CIG losses, LCM-LoRA backbone, training timestep restriction, and CAP inference with ControlNet/Canny guidance and skip-term removal are retained. Algorithm 1 corrects perturbation placement to match the latent-space attack already specified in v1 Equation 16; this does not establish a different method.

E1.justification: V3 Table 11 adds actual ImageNet evaluations under L2-PGD, StAdv, Snow, and Fog. These substantially broaden threat coverage, including weather-style input conditions beyond the previously evaluated attacks. ImageNet, CelebA-HQ, and the existing generation demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: The comparator membership is retained: GDMP becomes Wang et al., MS becomes Amini et al., and SCH becomes Singh et al.; DiffPure remains. Face-recognition comparators and the TCD comparison also remain. The new threat evaluations reuse DiffPure, and its revised scores do not establish a different comparison method.

E3.justification: V3 supplies protocols for the added attacks and changes the reported attack from PGD-10 to PGD-100 in Figure 5 and the skip-term ablation (v1 Table 6; v3 Table 8), despite unchanged displayed results. Its main DiffPure timing uses the stated F40 hardware instead of a borrowed V100 measurement. Core training settings and the 40,000/10,000 split remain; these changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix Table 11 substantially extends testing of generalization to unseen threats, accompanied by qualitative comparisons in Figure 10. Figure 4 adds visual evidence for image-quality comparisons. Conversely, v1's edge-blurring diagnostic and Figure 6 disappear. Existing Diff-PGD, component, timestep, and backbone analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both appendices specify PyTorch generator seed 100. V3 repeats fixed-seed evaluation in the main text, but neither version reports a changed run count, multiple-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces DiffPure's borrowed standard/robust accuracies of 67.79%/40.93% with 75.77%/73.02%, while OSCP remains at 77.63%/74.19%. V3 adds Table 11 results and substantially revises timings: at 1024×1024 and t*=500, appendix DiffPure timing changes from approximately 60 to 720 seconds and OSCP from 0.1 to 0.5 seconds. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V3 removes v1 Theorem 1 and its proof linking small training loss to purification error at cumulative alpha=0.5. The four appendix limit arguments remain, but Proof 2 adds the assumption beta at T/2 exceeds a positive constant and replaces the product bound. Proof 3 also revises its vanishing-term expression. These change substantive guarantees and mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline 74.19% accuracy, single evaluation, and 0.1-second purification claims remain. V3's abstract and conclusion explicitly quantify the efficiency claim as a 100-fold speedup, providing a limited refinement rather than a new central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds the argument that deterministic LCM inference makes Expectation over Transformation unnecessary, interprets OSCP as balancing purification and adversarial-training tradeoffs, and suggests adapting GAND to image-to-image tasks. The explicit limitation that purification strength requires time-consuming trial and error becomes a shorter future-work discussion.

D1.justification: V3 adds iteration counts, perturbation budgets, and step sizes for Fog, Snow, and L2-PGD. It removes v1's instruction to blur inputs before edge detection and the explicit DDIM-50 reproduction description for appendix DiffPure timings. Most training details and resource destinations remain, with footnote URLs converted to embedded hyperlinks. Omitted instructions do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: V3 adds references including Kaufmann et al. on unforeseen adversaries, Szegedy et al., and additional Guo et al. attacks, while removing several general computer-vision application references. It more explicitly positions OSCP as a hybrid defense. The central relationship to diffusion purification, consistency models, LoRA, and ControlNet remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Sections become numbered, GAND precedes CAP, preliminaries are condensed, and several appendix analyses enter dedicated main-text subsections. These substantially change the narrative and organization.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the opening illustration, combines the former pipeline and GAND diagrams into Figure 2, adds qualitative comparison panels, and removes the edge-blurring figure. Table 1 becomes a full-width comparison grouped by defense category. Several appendix tables move into the main text, existing plot panels are separated, and the appendix changes to two-column layout.

improvement.justification: V3 offers clearer organization and useful additional unseen-threat evidence. However, it removes preprocessing instructions and the main error-bound theorem while retaining text invoking a 'following theorem.' Substantial baseline revisions and changed ablation attack counts are insufficiently explained, and the earlier timing reproduction details disappear. These gains and losses leave the net effect on scientific support and reproducibility uncertain.
